title: Introduction
text: Welcome to Zanzibar SkyLab. Explore the sky from Stone Town, six degrees south of the equator. This demonstration uses a fixed observing date, so every calculated view is reproducible.

title: Sky Explorer
text: This is the real Sky Explorer. Select a catalogued star to inspect its calculated altitude and azimuth. Altitude measures height above the horizon. Azimuth gives the direction around it. Both depend on the observer's location and observing time. The inspector connects the sky map to the underlying astronomical calculations.

title: Astronomical Time Lab
text: The Astronomical Time Lab lets us explore how the sky changes. Watch the observing time advance in ten minute steps. Earth's rotation changes the local directions of stars. Solar time follows the Sun, while sidereal time refers to the stars. These are different reference directions, and they help explain the changing sky.

title: Observation Planner
text: The Observation Planner turns calculations into practical observing choices. We switch from Jupiter to Sirius, then compare another observing date. Calculated altitude curves show how high a target rises during the night. Twilight times help identify darker observing periods. Weather, terrain, and light pollution still affect what an observer can actually see.

title: Moon Explorer and Object Directory
text: The Moon Explorer shows lunar geometry and illumination. Illumination alone does not guarantee that a thin crescent will be visible. Next, the Object Directory connects catalogued objects to calculated sky positions. Searching for Sirius demonstrates how a familiar star can be found in the working observatory.

title: Innovation and conclusion
text: Five connected observatory tools, with astronomy calculated locally in your browser. Zanzibar SkyLab connects exploration with observation planning. Explore, calculate, plan, and observe. Thank you for visiting.
